claims.text: Equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr is a single-phase BCC solid solution in the as-cast or homogenized state.
As-cast or homogenized Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr has coarse grains.
Equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr has a density of approximately 11-12 g/cm³.
Severe plastic deformation followed by partial recrystallization will create a stable heterogeneous grain structure containing ultrafine or nanocrystalline grains and coarse grains.
An annealing range of approximately 800-1000 °C is likely to produce partial recrystallization without full grain coarsening in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
The heterogeneous grain structure creates internal back-stress fields through strain gradients between coarse- and fine-grained regions.
Strain incompatibility between ultrafine and coarse grains promotes deformation twinning in the coarse grains of Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
Back-stress strengthening from the heterogeneous grain structure elevates yield strength.
Deformation twinning in coarse grains delays necking and increases strain hardening and ductility.
Lattice distortion from the multi-principal-element composition provides baseline solid-solution strengthening.
The HGS-treated Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy will have a yield strength exceeding 1000 MPa.
The HGS-treated Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy will have total tensile elongation greater than 15% at room temperature.
HGS treatment will simultaneously improve yield strength and room-temperature ductility relative to coarse-grained Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
HGS processing will maintain density comparable to the baseline BCC solid solution.
As-cast equiatomic Ti-Zr-Hf-Nb-Ta has a yield strength of approximately 830 MPa.
As-cast or homogenized equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr typically has less than 5% room-temperature ductility.
Low room-temperature ductility in the baseline alloy is caused by limited slip systems and high Peierls stress in its BCC structure.
Excessive annealing causes grain coarsening, removes the back-stress mechanism, and restores brittle coarse-grained behavior.
Severe plastic deformation or annealing may form brittle B2 or Laves phases in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr and negate ductility gains.

contradictions.description: The initial state identifies high density as a limitation, but the boundary field says the composition addresses that limitation while also conceding that no density reduction is claimed. Maintaining the same high density does not internally substantiate the statement that the limitation is addressed.
The defined alloy contains Hf, Mo, Ta, Ti, and Zr, whereas the boundary's density explanation lists W as one of its heavy constituent elements even though W is absent from the proposed composition.
